quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
rationale: Section 13 contains a Vendor-side IP indemnity: Garman warrants it owns/controls all rights necessary and indemnifies Sparkling (and its officers and directors) against all Losses, including legal fees and settlement amounts, arising from breach of that warranty, with the usual infringement remedies of procuring rights, replacing or modifying the affected element (p0091–p0093). There is no reciprocal Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software, and Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability limitation, so the indemnity is uncapped — better than the fallback's 3× annual fees super-cap. This sits at the playbook fallback: it does not extend to Garman's breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct, there is no express duty to defend, the refund remedy is absent, and the ten-calendar-day notice window is tighter than we would prefer. Those are sub-elements short of the preferred position and are noted rather than redlined.

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
rationale: The agreement imposes no exclusivity, sole-supplier or minimum-requirements obligation on Sparkling, which meets the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer). We searched the licence grant (§2), use restrictions (§3), maintenance and support (§10), fees (§11) and the general/boilerplate provisions, and ran targeted searches for "exclusive", "sole", "requirements from", "procure", "supplier", "competitor" and "third party". The only occurrences of "exclusive" are benign or favourable to us: the licence grant and the source-code escrow licence are expressly non-exclusive (p0028, p0115), §15 contains a mutual exclusive-remedy provision (p0105), and the jurisdiction clause is non-exclusive (p0146). The §3 use restrictions are ordinary software-licence limitations (copying, reverse engineering, sublicensing) and do not restrict our right to buy competing products or engage third-party maintainers. Nothing requires us to source software, maintenance or support solely from Garman, so we retain full freedom to procure from other suppliers. No redline is required.

quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "interest" and "shall pay" return no provision imposing liquidated damages, penalties, late-payment interest, accelerated fees or a minimum/early-termination fee on Sparkling. Section 11 obliges Sparkling only to pay fees per the Fee Schedule; Section 17(b) permits termination for convenience on 90 days' notice with no exit payment; Section 17 (p0128) in fact runs in our favour (perpetual licence and refund of prepaid fees on Garman's default). Section 15 limits damages to direct damages for both parties, and the mutual non-solicitation in Section 19 carries no stipulated payment. This meets the preferred position of no liquidated damages or penalties payable by the Customer, so no redline is required.

rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use covenant binds Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement. Section 3 (Restrictions on Use) is limited to ordinary software-licence use restrictions (no copying beyond backup/internal use, no assignment or sublicence, no reverse engineering, use only as authorised) and does not restrict the businesses Sparkling may operate or the products it may buy or build. Searches for "compet", "similar software", "develop", "exclusiv" and "shall not" return only a non-exclusive licence grant, confidentiality carve-outs (including independent development, which preserves our freedom to develop), and boilerplate. Section 19 is a mutual one-year non-solicitation of employees, not a non-compete, and it binds Garman equally. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is required.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: Section 17(b) gives us (Sparkling) an unqualified right to terminate for convenience at any time on ninety (90) days' written notice, and no early-termination fee or penalty is imposed anywhere (Section 11 and the Fee Schedule reference no exit charge). Garman has no corresponding convenience right: its only termination rights arise under Section 17(c) on insolvency or uncured material default, which satisfies the preferred position that the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term. The clause therefore sits at the fallback on notice period (60–90 days rather than the preferred 30 days) and better than fallback on fees, so it is compliant and we do not redline it. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted only: the 90-day notice is at the outer edge of the fallback range, and Section 17(b) contains no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees (refund of fees for services not yet rendered is expressly provided only on termination for Garman's default under Section 17(c)). If the agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would seek 30 days' notice and an express pro-rata refund.

quote: (e) not use the Work except as authorized herein;
rationale: Searches for audit, inspection, verification, examination, records, premises, remote/system access and compliance-check language return no right for Garman to audit or verify Sparkling's use. The use restrictions in § 3 (a)-(g) impose no reporting or verification mechanic, § 14 (Confidentiality) only addresses mutual protection of information, and the only inspection right in the document runs in our favour (§ 16 escrow: "Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials"). With no vendor audit right at all, there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to constrain — the position is better than the playbook's preferred (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, vendor cost, no system access), so nothing is redlined. We should resist any vendor attempt to add an audit or usage-verification right in negotiation; if one is introduced, it must carry the preferred limits.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: Searches for MFN-style language ("most favoured nation", "no less favourable", "favorable/favourable", "best price", "lowest", "other customers", "discount", "third party") return nothing of the kind, and the only plausible homes for such language are silent: the Fees section (sec-11, p0084) is a bare obligation to pay the Fee Schedule amounts, the maintenance pricing provisions (sec-10) simply cross-refer to the Fee Schedule, and General Matters (sec-20) covers only time of the essence and notices. Sparkling is therefore under no obligation to extend Garman terms no less favourable than those given to any third party, and there is no obligation to match third-party offers. rationale: There is no automatic-renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement. Maintenance runs for a "renewable one-year term" (p0065), i.e. renewal for a further 12 months requires the parties to agree and Sparkling to elect to pay the renewal maintenance fees; the licence itself is perpetual so long as fees are paid (p0117), and Sparkling may in any event exit on ninety (90) days' notice at any time (p0118). That matches the preferred position (renewal by mutual agreement, 12-month periods, no evergreen lock-in and no non-renewal notice window to compute), and it is more favourable to us than the fallback. The only preferred sub-element absent is an express cap on renewal-fee uplift (lesser of CPI and 3%) — the Fee Schedule contains no escalation language at all, so there is no unilateral uplift right for Garman to exercise; we note this rather than flagging it, and would seek a CPI/3% cap on renewal maintenance fees if the Fee Schedule is reopened.

verification.notes: precision position: preferred transition includes standard machine-readable format: State standard machine-readable format expressly in the transition obligation. precision position: preferred transition includes 30-day return after expiry or termination: State 30-day return after expiry or termination expressly in the transition obligation. The inserted paragraph (d) supplies every preferred atomic element: assistance on expiry or termination, up to six months, at then-current rates, 30-day data return, machine-readable format, deletion after return, and written certification of deletion. "commonly used, machine-readable format" is the functional equivalent of the playbook's "standard machine-readable format"; the deterministic flag on this point is a wording nuance to note in the rationale, not a material gap. The 30-day return clock runs from "expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason", not from a request; the "at Sparkling's request" condition attaches only to limb (i) transition assistance and does not swallow the mandatory data-return or deletion/certification duties. Drafting is a concise single-paragraph insertion into a document that previously had no vendor-side exit/data-return duty, so it is minimal; no untouched sentence is altered and all surviving-provision and perpetual-licence mechanics remain effective. Inclusion of "Confidential Information" alongside data broadens the return/deletion scope in our favour and "reasonable" mildly qualifies assistance; neither is an offending extra nor adverse to us. Because the clause meets the preferred position, the fallback (90 days / 30-day export) is also comfortably exceeded; no further redline is warranted.

quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
rationale: Section 12 gives an express conformance-to-Specifications warranty for the acceptance period plus one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and continuing for as long as the Software is under Maintenance Services — this meets and in fact exceeds the preferred 12-month software warranty. A real remedy exists: Garman must repair non-conforming Software at no additional charge under the Software Repair Service (p0077), and during acceptance testing Sparkling may reject the Software and recover "any and all amounts paid to Garman hereunder" (p0053, p0057). There is no "AS IS" language and no disclaimer of implied warranties anywhere in the agreement, so nothing swallows the express warranty; the Section 15 liability cap preserves recovery of direct damages. Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted but not flagged: there is no separate professional-and-workmanlike services warranty covering installation, training and maintenance, no no-malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty, and post-acceptance repair is qualified by "best efforts" without an express replace-or-refund alternative. These are drafting refinements we may raise conversationally rather than material failures.

rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns no results, and General Matters (§ 20, subsections (a)–(i) at p0135–p0147) contains no insurance covenant, so no usable clause exists anywhere in the Agreement. The rule is triggered because Garman is not a pure software licensor: it installs the Software on AS400s at each Authorized Location and performs future installations at Sparkling's sites (p0041, p0042), and it converts "Sparkling's data ... from its current electronic form" (p0042), plus training and ongoing maintenance. A vendor that both works on our premises and processes our data with no insurance at all sits in walk-away territory under this rule, well short of even the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M). We therefore insert a short preferred-position insurance paragraph as new § 20(j), the smallest edit that cures the gap, drafted with "Sparkling's data" rather than "Customer Data" since that term is not defined in this Agreement, and noting the fallback limits in the comment.

quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement. No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
rationale: Section 13 is the only ownership provision. It gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work including the Schedule "D" Modifications we pay for, and sweeps in "all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement" without limiting that to Garman-supplied materials — which on its face could capture our own materials and the data Garman converts under Section 4(b). There is no statement anywhere in the Agreement that we retain rights in our data. Garman keeping its platform is acceptable, but the fallback is not met either: the only licence back (Section 2) is a non-exclusive, non-transferable use licence tied to Authorized Locations and continued fee payment, with no modify or sublicence rights and no express coverage of the funded Modifications. Redline limits Garman's ownership claim to its own materials, adds a Customer-data ownership sentence, and adds a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Modifications we fund; we have not sought assignment of the Modifications given the packaged-software bargain and the Section 16 source code arrangements.

quote: The parties agree that the limitation of liability in this paragraph reflects the allocation of risk between the parties and the price of the licenced Software. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.
rationale: Section 15 is the only liability provision in the Agreement (Sections 11–14 contain no cap or aggregate liability language). It mutually excludes indirect and consequential damages and disapplies its limitations to Sections 13 (IP) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap of any kind, so each party — including Sparkling — bears unlimited exposure for direct damages. That fails the fallback, which requires a mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees. We therefore added the preferred mutual cap (greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000), kept the existing Section 13/14 carve-outs and extended them to indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmed that Sparkling's fee obligations are not capped "damages". The mutual exclusion of consequential damages already meets the preferred position and is left untouched.

quote: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
rationale: Section 19 binds us as well as the Vendor, but it is a no-hire ("agree not to hire ... any employee of the other party"), not a non-solicit, and its first limb covers all of the other party's employees rather than only those involved in the services. There is also no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions and restrictions covering all personnel are walk-away items under this rule, so the clause fails the fallback. The redline converts it into a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the services with the customary carve-outs, landing at the fallback position.
